Off-machine copy A verified bundle of every branch, plus uncommitted work and transcripts, copied off the PC nightly. Protects against the unexpected power-offs and disk loss.Bottleneck B11; harness v2 phase 1.
One budget The rule that all agent-adding changes share a single written token and lane budget: two S lanes at a time, one change that adds agents per window, state on disk.Harness v2 section 6; the refuter warned remedies together recreate the stops.
One fact, one command A rule that an environment fact reported by an agent or stated by me is checked by one command before it becomes a harness rule.Harness v2 mechanism 7, from five facts the bottleneck list got wrong.
Open-risks list Claims that were neither verified nor refuted, kept together with the test that would settle each one.Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.
Orchestrator (root, main session) The long-lived top session that plans, briefs, reads results and diffs, judges gates, merges and edits shared files. Its window is the largest token cost we measured.A Claude Code session role; named in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10 and the clinic orchestration.
Output shapes (MAP, RESEARCH, FINDINGS, VERDICT, COMMANDS, SCAN) Fixed schemas agents return. FINDINGS is an analyst's ranked claims, VERDICT a skeptic's ruling, and SCAN reports committed secrets as fingerprints.Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10, section 5.2.
Owner decision A choice only I can make, such as installing a tool or allowing a sensor logger. Listed as D01 to D23 with a default and what it unlocks.Harness v2 decision table; the [owner] step in plans.
Owner step A step only I may perform; agents stop there. Written as [owner] in plans and skills.Coined by us in .claude/skills/README.md.
OWNER-VIEW.md My one-line-per-phase status page, updated when a phase closes.Coined by us in the ship plan.
Pathway map A model of the library as a graph of states work passes through, with chances and costs on each branch. It shows the mechanism; its figures are model outputs from guessed inputs G, not a forecast.Coined by us; built in docs/program/library-pathways/, 2026-11.
Per-lane database A database private to one lane's checkout, with its own port and compose project, so parallel checks cannot corrupt each other.Testbed isolation design; restarted by the restart chain.
Pilot backlog / T15-T17 Findings moved out of the gates to be fixed during the pilot. T15, T16 and T17 are plan acceptance targets; T17 covers page latency and load.My decision USER-24; clinic technical plan.
Plan @ sha First line of a phase PR body naming the exact commit of the ship plan in force. A resumed session re-reads the plan diff from that commit.Our rule, adopted through the Horthy sweep and harness review ruling HR-C2.
Plan tags (plan-v9, plan-v9.1) Git tags on plan commits so a lane reads exactly the commit it cites.Coined by us in SHIP-PLAN section 7.1.
Planner / Scheduler / Governor Planner picks the lane count before work starts. Scheduler starts and resumes sessions. Governor slows the lanes so the five-hour usage window lasts. All three are harness v2 designs.Coined by us in the harness v2 design.
PR #183 The pull request holding the knowledge-store design. The store is designed, not proven.This repository on GitHub.
PR #184 / PR #186 The pull requests holding the BAML sweep (#184) and the Horthy sweep (#186), with our verdict on each idea.This repository on GitHub.
PR #185 The pull request, merged on 13 November, that added 13 M skill packages and 11 M fixflow agents.This repository on GitHub.
PR journal (PR-body journal) The running record of decisions, evidence and session ids that a phase keeps in its draft pull request’s description, so a later session can resume from it.Our ship-plan practice; the harness review calls it the PR-body journal.
Probe / mutant / probe-in-lookup / valid_when / tri-state verdict A probe is a small automatic check that a root cause is present; a mutant is a harmless edit it must ignore. valid_when is a precondition. Verdicts: applies, not_applies, inconclusive.Coined by us; mutant idea from mutation testing in software testing.
PROJECT CONTEXT block A fixed piece of text placed before every subagent prompt, giving the repository, branch, settled facts and rules.Coined by us in the orchestration design and clinic launcher.
Promoted checks Mechanical checks from stored entries moved into the shared test run, so every piece of work passes them with no lookup.Coined by us; the knowledge-store design D17 drains entries into CI.
Queue In our work, a line of waiting items: the check slot queue with a printed position, the merge queue, or the phone's write queues. Context says which.Bottleneck B07 (fair queue); mobile queues in CLAUDE.md.
Quiet window (quiet machine) A time when no FixFlow phase is running or waiting on its reviewer and no heavy check holds a slot on this PC, so a harness check or agent run cannot slow the ship lanes.Our own term in this compile, from the harness v2 rule that the ship plan comes first.
Reader / reducer / pre-registration / arm / gates G0-G5 Reader extracts; reducer re-fetches and checks quotes. Pre-registration fixes test, gates and budget in writing before running. An arm is one condition in a comparison. G0-G5 are research checkpoints.Our map programme run.md; pre-registration and arm come from scientific method.
Reader’s check An agent on a fixed prompt reads a brief or a compaction summary twice and marks each statement of the latest state right or wrong, and each open loop carried or dropped.The split rule (WP12), part 6.4.
Real-host rehearsal Running the first-deploy checklist on a real host: fresh-machine restore, off-site push, an alert with a planted failure. Each step has a command, expected result and failing run.Bottleneck B19; harness v2 phase 4.
Reaper (dry-run reaper) A cleanup script that removes finished sessions or worktrees. It runs as a dry run first, only reporting what it would remove.Coined by us in the bottleneck compile, for bottleneck B15.
Reasoning-cache library (the library) A proposed separate memory of verified solutions that a cheap model fetches, adapts and reuses instead of calling a stronger model. Designed and modelled in the pathway map; not built or proven.Coined by me; described in the harness v2 design and library pathway documents, 2026-11.
Record-only mode A script mode that writes down what it would refuse or flag but blocks nothing, so it can be validated before it gets power.Coined by us in the bottleneck compile, section 9.3.
Refuter (refute-by-default) A fresh-context agent, usually Opus at high effort, whose job is to disprove a claim, fix or design. It treats the claim as wrong until code, tests or sources show otherwise.Coined by us in the orchestration method and harness sweeps.
Register (bottleneck register) The one list of every bottleneck our sessions found, 128 M in all, joined and de-duplicated in Part 2; each row has a family, a state and the work package that answers it. Not the findings register of FixFlow’s reviews.This compile, 13 November 2026. It joins the bottleneck compile’s B01 to B21, the harness v2 loops, the Dex Horthy sweep’s weaknesses and levers, and the ids added here.
Replay before live A gate or review mechanism is accepted by replaying it on the recorded history first, record-only, before it may refuse anything live.Harness v2 standing principle with script before agent and one budget.
Restart chain Proposed: Docker starts at sign-in, the databases in use restart themselves, and the check starts its own database if missing, so work resumes after a power-off without commands. Parked for now, because I chose to keep Docker’s start at sign-in off (D03); the resume list therefore starts with “start Docker”.Bottleneck B10 and decision D03; nothing restarted in the three idle days.
Resume list At sign-in, a list of sessions that were mid-work and where each branch stands. Sessions are released two S at a time; a mismatched record parks itself.Bottleneck B03 and decision D06.
Review round One pass in which a reviewer reads a branch and returns findings, followed by fixes. The harness aims to cap rounds at two T.Testbed record: 2.8 rounds per slice M; fix-round contract target.
Route A / Route B Two ways BAML could run here. A: claude -p with Claude Code's own tools, on the subscription. B: API-keyed typed functions with hand-written tools.Coined by us in the BAML structural comparison.
RT-01..RT-09 Named failure shapes from the clinic record about verification that goes green without testing anything. RT-01: a check must be able to fail. RT-06: unknown is not zero.Clinic testbed task records; harness review section 4.
Save-as-run rule Every workflow is saved as a script before it runs, so it can be re-run and its result checked against the saved version.Our orchestration design; adopted through WP10a.
Scores E/T/N/B/C The BAML assessment's five 0-to-3 scores: evidence quality, transferability, novelty, expected benefit, and cost and risk (3 means cheap and safe).Coined by us in the BAML sweep.
Script-first rule Prefer deterministic scripts over prompts or model re-checks to guard quality, because prose rules and re-checks did not hold in the testbed.Coined by us in the bottleneck compile, section 7.
Scripted search The search baseline run as a fixed script. No agent decided what to search, and no agent was run in the held-out test.Wording fixed by us in graph2 protocol addendum 6, 2026-11.
Sealed replay / replay seal Re-running a recorded fix chain or review at a frozen commit, in a clone with no later refs and a hashed answer key, so the agent cannot see the fix.Coined by us in the bottleneck compile, sections 4 and 9.3.
Seed / reference (graph test) The seed is the changed file or symbol given as the query. The reference is the other files and definitions the same commit changed.Coined by us in graph2/protocol.md, 2026-11.
Send-back A reviewer returning a slice to its author with findings to fix, instead of passing it to merge. Each send-back adds a review round.Testbed review loop; the fix-round contract limits how many are allowed.
Seven metrics Throughput, efficiency, token count, token cost, time taken, quality of output and hallucinations: what I judge every bottleneck and idea by. Part 2 defines each.My correction of 14 November 2026.
Silent runner / g() A wrapper that writes full test logs to a file and prints one line. Our g() in Appendix A does this for backend checks.Idea from HumanLayer's hack/run_silent.sh; our g() is coined by us in Appendix A.
Single-writer rule Only the root session edits shared documents.Coined by us in the clinic orchestration page.
Skeptic A fresh-context Opus verifier given only a claim, its evidence and its failing condition, and asked to trace or refute it. The number of skeptics per gate is capped.Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.
Slice One bounded unit of build work with its own branch, worktree and record, checked, reviewed and merged. Slice sessions used 66.4 % M of November tokens.Vertical-slice practice; used in the clinic wave plan (S00-S12).
Spatial / temporal recall Spatial: a thing's neighbourhood in code and work. Temporal: when a fact became true and when it was replaced. Both are ways to look things up.Coined by us in HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS-2026-11, section 6, 2026-11.
Split and merge (of sessions) / split line In my B+ tree proposal (PAR-22), sessions are nodes of a distributed system: leaves do the work, inner ones route and gate. One whose window passes the split line hands its work, by scope, to two fresh sessions (a hand-over), and two small siblings join into one. The line is a share of the window, set per model; about 40 % S is the outside rule of thumb, 400k E on our windows.My proposal of 14 November 2026; the 40 % figure came with the Dex Horthy sweep and is untested here.
Staleness When a stored entry may no longer be true because the code changed. Handled by validity conditions and probes, not by time-based expiry.Knowledge-store design; time expiry is on the do-not-build list.
Standing rules 1-7, R1-R10, HR-A1..A4 The plan's section 0 rules, my rulings and the human-review amendments, which the parallel-execution section leaves unchanged.Coined by us in the v8 ship plan and the harness review.
Status codes V/S/C/G/O Register statuses: V skeptic-confirmed, S skeptic-narrowed, C corroborated, G gap or design, O open.Coined by us at gate G2.
Stub / stub harness A fake stand-in for agent() that returns canned results (nothing, throw, refute) so a script's bookkeeping is tested with no model, at zero tokens.General software testing; our item S-3 in the BAML sweep. Pydantic AI TestModel is prior art.
Sweep A study that goes through one outside body of work idea by idea (each idea a card), scores every idea against our own weaknesses, sends the scores to refuters and sorts the survivors into adopt, trial and drop lists. We ran two: BAML (PR #184) and Dex Horthy (PR #186).Our own term, from the sweeps of 4 and 9 November 2026.
Synthetic seeder / SYN token A script that creates fake test data. Real labels without the SYN marker are refused by design.Coined by us in the clinic build.
T1 / T1x / T2 / T3 / T4 / T5 / TQ Graph-test task sets: T1 change completion; T1x its cross-runtime subset; T2 changed code to tests; T3 documented chains; T4 defect register; T5 document lookups; TQ code-reading questions.Coined by us in graph2/protocol.md, 2026-11.
Task ID scheme (H-01, S-01a, R-01, O-01) H is a Haiku extractor, S a Sonnet mapper or gate runner, R a research agent, O an Opus analyst. The numbers are stable labels used for resume.Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.
theta_lead, theta_cand, mu Planned retrieval thresholds: lead at 0.5 S, candidate at 0.3 S, margin 0.2 S. They decide lead, candidate or miss and are to be frozen at KS-4.Coined by us (decision D8) in KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md.
Three conditions (comes back, reach, entry quality) Comes back: much work repeats. Reach: an entry gets to the cheap model. Entry quality: the entry is right and used rightly. A fourth group is running cost.Coined by us in model-brief.md revision 4, 2026-11.
Three ways of working (policies) Strong model directly (top_first), cheap model with the ladder (cheap_ladder), and cheap model with the library. All three run on the same pieces of work.Coined by us in library-pathways model-brief.md, 2026-11.
Trace / early cutoff / control pair / inject-control Trace: fingerprint of the footprint at the last passing check. Early cutoff: keep an entry if its check still passes after a dependency changed. Control pair: two commits where the check must read present, then absent. Inject-control re-applies the failing pattern.Trace and early cutoff from Build Systems a la Carte (ICFP 2018); controls coined by us.
Transcript audit A script reading the sessions' own tool-call records to show who read the final head, whether the gate ran before each fix, and root edits per merge.Harness v2 script 3; replayed over the 10 and 11 November merges.
Typed code store A map of the code whose edges are labelled by kind (import, caller, test-of, crosses-runtime) rather than file-level imports only. Tried in the second graph test design.My objections to the first graph test; replacement test protocol.
Typed verdict A review result in a fixed machine-readable form that names the head commit the reviewer read. See also Output shapes and Verdicts.Coined by us in the bottleneck compile.
UPSTREAM.md and SPDX licence UPSTREAM.md records where a sourced skill package came from: repository, commit, paths, licence, date. SPDX is the standard short licence identifier, for example MIT.UPSTREAM.md is ours (.claude/skills/README.md); SPDX is an outside standard.
USER-21 to USER-24 My numbered decisions on the clinic board: 21, the root may start the next slices itself; 22, approve a parallel-test dependency; 23, use the machine and a Linux container; 24, wrap up the build.My decision log of the clinic build.
Verdict script A script that closes or reopens a gate round without a model: for each closed P1 citing a test, it runs the test at the fix's parent and counts failures.Harness v2 script 2; checked by a replay on the record.
Verdicts: CONFIRMED, PARTIALLY, REFUTED, UNVERIFIABLE The four skeptic outcomes. Unverifiable means neither proven nor disproven, and it carries the test that would settle it.Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.
W0, W1, W2, S3 (stages) Investigation stage names: W0 my pre-flight with no agents, W1 wide cheap discovery, W2 narrow expensive deep dive, S3 the later phase plan.Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.
W1-W5 (weaknesses) The five weaknesses ideas were scored against: W1 CLAUDE.md length, W2 self-reported compliance, W3 routine never run (cold resume), W4 few agents and skills, W5 workflows not saved. Not the W0-W2 stages.Coined by us in HARNESS-IDEAS-HORTHY-2026-11.md.
Wave A group of slices or lanes run in parallel once their dependencies have merged. Ship plan waves A to D set the order lanes start.Coined by us in the clinic build and SHIP-PLAN-2026-11 section 7.6.
What-is-true-now board A generated view of slices, verdicts and findings, each with the commit it became true at and the commit that replaced it. Replaces the hand-edited board.Harness v2 library first half; board target under 20 KB T from 221 KB M.
Work package (WP) A self-contained piece of harness work a team member can pick up from the PDF, with its goal, steps and a test that says it is done.This compile's hand-off format for readers who were not in the sessions.
Write gate / diff lookup / false-fire ceiling / caller-pin test / second door Write gate: checks on recording. Diff lookup (ks lookup --diff): warns when a PR touches protected code. False-fire ceiling: one commit in ten T. Caller-pin test: fixes allowed callers. Second door: a path that skips a guard.Coined by us (KS-2, D8, D17; my critique, 2026-11-03).
Zero-seed journey / walk A first-use walk on an empty database with no synthetic data: first user, import, a transaction, and close of day.Coined by us in the clinic testbed work.

Claude Code and Anthropic

Agent definition (.claude/agents, agentType) A markdown file that names a helper agent with its own prompt, tools and pinned model, selected through agentType or subagent_type. We have 11 M fixflow-* agents.Claude Code subagents feature.
anthropic-skills:code-audit An existing generic security-audit skill that our appsec-review-asvs skill package builds on.Listed among the skills available to our Claude Code sessions.
API call (message id) One request to the model, which re-reads the whole window. The message id is its unique id, used to count each call once.Anthropic API.
Auto-memory Agent-written memory notes that Claude Code loads at the start of each session (15 M files in the clinic root).A Claude Code feature.
autoCompactWindow (auto-compact window) A Claude Code setting, 100000 to 1000000 tokens S, naming the size that triggers automatic compaction. A setting of 400000 S compacts near 367k M.Claude Code setting (/autocompact).
Bypass mode A Claude Code permission mode in which subagents run without asking for approval.Claude Code feature.
Cache read (cache-read tokens) Tokens re-read from the prompt cache on each call at a lower price. Summed over calls they show how much context is carried: 4,253M M in November.Anthropic API prompt caching.
Cache write (cache creation tokens) Tokens newly stored in the prompt cache, counted separately from cache reads.Anthropic API prompt caching.
claude -p Claude Code's non-interactive command-line mode: one process per prompt.Claude Code feature.
Claude Code Anthropic's coding agent that runs in a terminal or desktop app. Our harness is the set of rules, scripts and checks built around its sessions.Anthropic product; the tool all our sessions run in.
CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md Project instruction files an agent session reads first. FixFlow's is long, so every session pays to read it; AGENTS.md is the equivalent convention for other agent tools.CLAUDE.md is a Claude Code feature; AGENTS.md is an agent-tool convention.
Compaction Claude Code replacing a long conversation with a summary, plus a verbatim tail, so the session can continue. We counted 48 M in main sessions in November.Claude Code feature.
Compaction summary The summary left after compaction, re-read on every later call. It was 8 % M of context tokens in the study.Claude Code feature.
cost-state Claude Code’s own spend counter (not our harness’s). Its totals are a lower bound, covering about one third E of the work.Claude Code’s cost-state file, as described in the token-spend README.
Effort levels (low, medium, high, xhigh) A per-agent setting for how much reasoning a model spends. We raise it before moving up a model tier; xhigh is the highest and costs the most.Claude Code and Anthropic model setting.
Explore agent Claude Code's built-in file-finding agent. It inherits the model tier of the session that starts it.Claude Code feature.
Fast mode A Claude Code setting that returns output faster on the models that support it.Claude Code feature.
Frontmatter and skills preload Frontmatter is the header block of an agent file; its skills field loads the named skill's full text when the agent starts.Claude Code.
get_usage and /context get_usage reports a session's tokens used and compactions. /context shows what fills the window: skills, connectors, CLAUDE.md.Claude Code desktop and command-line features.
Hook (PreCompact, SessionStart, PostCompact, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) A script Claude Code runs automatically at an event, such as before compaction, at session start or on stop. It can add text, block, or alter a tool call.Claude Code feature.
Idle compaction A compaction that uses a summary precomputed while the session sat idle. Default on, with a threshold of 200k tokens S.Claude Code setting idleCompaction.
MCP / connector Model Context Protocol, a standard for plugging tools and data sources into Claude. A connector is a linked outside service whose tool definitions add to window size.Open standard from Anthropic; used by Claude Code.
permissions.deny A block in the project's .claude/settings.json that lists commands the agent may not run.Claude Code feature.
Prompt caching A feature that stores a repeated prompt start so later calls can read it cheaply.Anthropic API feature.
Scratchpad A session-specific temporary folder outside the repository where agents write logs and working files.Claude Code session environment.
SendMessage and parked start SendMessage sends a message to a running session. A parked start is a session created now and released later by a message.SendMessage is a Claude Code tool; parked start is ours (card CR-02).
Session One running Claude Code conversation with its own context window and tools. Ours come as orchestrator, coordinator and lane sessions; each starts fresh and can be parked or resumed.Claude Code usage; the unit every harness rule is written for.
Session transcript (JSONL) The saved record of a Claude Code session, one JSON line per message or call, pruned after 30 days S by default. JSONL is the one-record-per-line format.Claude Code feature; JSON Lines is a general format.
Skill (SKILL.md) A folder of instructions an agent loads for a kind of task, starting with a SKILL.md whose description says when to use it. We have 13 M skill packages.Claude Code feature; our conventions are in .claude/skills/README.md.
StructuredOutput The forced tool call a schema-bearing subagent must make to return its answer. The tool layer validates it and asks for a retry if it does not match.Claude Code Workflow feature.
Subagent A separate Claude agent started by a session or workflow to do one task and return a result. Each pays a fixed prefix cost before it starts work.Claude Code feature.
Tool and connector schemas (deferred schemas) Descriptions of every tool and connector loaded into the window. Deferred schemas list tools by name only and load full text when needed, shrinking the prefix.Claude Code and MCP features.
ToolSearch, WebFetch, WebSearch Claude Code tools. The web tools must be loaded through ToolSearch before an agent can use them.Claude Code tools.
Ultracode Claude Code’s multi-agent working mode: with it on, a session runs workflows of many agents by default, so token cost multiplies and the model and effort chosen for each agent matter.Claude Code (Anthropic); used throughout ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.
updatedToolOutput A PostToolUse hook route that replaces a tool's result before the model sees it.Claude Code feature, as recorded in our runtime audit.
Usage limit (five-hour window) The plan's cap on use within a rolling five-hour period S. When it is reached, all work stops. How cache reads count against it is not yet known.Anthropic plan feature.
Workflow (workflow script, agent()) A saved JavaScript script run by the Workflow tool. It issues subagents in a set order with agent(prompt, {schema, model, effort}) and returns one structured result.Claude Code workflow feature.
Workflow run journal (journal.jsonl, resumeFromRunId, knownDead) A per-run log of finished agent results that lets a stopped workflow resume from its run id; knownDead lists ids that returned null last time. Not the same as the knowledge store’s journal of event files.Claude Code workflow feature; the knownDead use is ours.

Models

Fable The model that runs the main session as orchestrator, architect and judge. It is not run as a subagent.An Anthropic model; its role was set in docs/ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md.
Haiku The smallest, cheapest Anthropic tier here, used only for typed extraction and for locating where code lives (the fixflow-explorer agent).Anthropic model family.
Hallucination A model stating something that is not so: a report that overstates what was done, an invented fact, path or API, or a wrong summary after compaction.General language-model field; one of my seven metrics.
List price ratio 80:40:20:1 The relative list price of new tokens, Fable to Opus to Sonnet to Haiku S, used to turn model calls into cheap-call equivalents in the library model.Outside price list, checked 2026-11-12 and recorded in the library review memory note.
Model tier A model's rung on the ladder from Haiku to Sonnet to Opus to Fable: higher tiers think better and cost more per token. We route work by tier.Anthropic naming; our routing memory note assigns jobs to tiers.
Opus The strongest Anthropic tier in routine use here: deep subsystem analysis, architects, refuters, skeptics, critics and fresh-context checks. With our compaction setting it compacts near 367k tokens M.Anthropic model family.
reasoning_extraction refusal A billed Anthropic API reply (HTTP 200, stop_reason refusal) that can come back when a schema asks for the model's own reasoning. Ask for an explanation instead.Anthropic API documentation on structured outputs.
Sonnet The mid-tier Anthropic model used for discovery, mapping, web collection, scouts, citation checks, gates and blind readers; the cheap model in the library plan.Anthropic model family.
Thinking tokens Tokens a model spends reasoning before it answers. They count as output tokens and so as usage, even though the reasoning is not shown in the reply.Model behaviour; counted inside output tokens in our token measurements.

Outside people, tools and ideas

@assert / @check / Collector BAML rules: @assert rejects a bad value; @check records a named pass or fail and keeps the value. The Collector records every attempt per call.BoundaryML's BAML (Collector added in 0.79.0).
12-factor agents / ACE / ACP / GenSX Outside agent-engineering projects that the clinic audited alongside HumanLayer's work.Outside projects.
AI That Works A weekly show hosted by Vaibhav Gupta (BoundaryML, the BAML company) and Dex Horthy; 582 M of the 1,906 M sweep cards come from its episodes.Outside series; hosts as named in the Horthy sweep and the BAML sweep.
Aider An open-source coding agent that runs in the terminal. Its repo map, a ranked outline of a codebase’s files and symbols sent to the model, is one source of our code-map ideas.Outside open-source project.
Anthropic The company that makes the Claude models and Claude Code. Its usage limit and price list set the budget the harness works within.Outside vendor; source of models, limits and list prices.
Backpressure Scripts and checks that push back on an agent with short failure output, so errors reach it cheaply and noise stays out of its context.Dex Horthy, HumanLayer blog post "Context-Efficient Backpressure for Coding Agents", 2025-12-09.
BAML A language for typed LLM functions that turn model replies into typed objects. We assessed it for generic ideas and did not adopt the tool (PR #184). v0 is the legacy domain-specific language (DSL); v1 has not yet reached 1.0.BoundaryML, an outside company.
BFCL / constrained decoding / schema-echo / TOON BFCL: Berkeley function-calling leaderboard. Constrained decoding forces tokens to fit a grammar and needs logit access. Schema-echo: the reply repeats the schema. TOON: a compact input text format.UC Berkeley benchmark; general LLM field; terms discussed in BAML's evaluations.
BoundaryML The company that makes BAML. Its podcast, post-mortems and benchmarks were quoted in our BAML sweep.Outside company.
ClaudeCodeClient / canary / nightly A BAML v1 client, available only in the canary channel, that runs one claude -p process per turn. Canary and nightly are BAML's pre-release channels; v1 has no stable release.BoundaryML.
Codex / gpt-6-astra Codex is OpenAI’s coding agent; our tools were tested with it as a second target, and it was proposed as an outside second reviewer (not adopted). gpt-6-astra is the model name in the Codex evaluation runs.Outside vendor product (OpenAI).
Colab / Kaggle Free hosted notebook services with GPU time limits. Long training runs there can be cut off, much as a session limit stops an agent.Google (Colab) and Kaggle, outside services.
Context engineering Deciding what goes into a session's context and what stays out, so the model stays useful. Horthy's name for the craft behind our hot set and library ideas.Dex Horthy and HumanLayer; sweep recorded in PR #186.
dependency-cruiser / import-linter Tools that fail the build when code crosses forbidden module boundaries: dependency-cruiser for JavaScript, import-linter for Python.Outside open-source tools.
Dex Horthy Outside practitioner at HumanLayer, author of the 12-Factor Agents repository and the research-plan-implement (RPI) skills, whose published work since 2025-06-01 we swept for harness ideas (PR #186).Outside person; the HumanLayer company and its public repositories.
DuckDB / DuckPGQ DuckDB is an embedded analytical SQL database; DuckPGQ is its extension that adds property-graph queries.DuckDB project and a community extension.
Dumb zone Horthy's name for the stretch of a long context window where quality degrades. Horthy set it at 100k tokens S in mid-2025, then withdrew the flat figure.Outside person (Dex Horthy).
FalkorDB / Apache AGE Two more graph databases we could run through Docker: FalkorDB is a graph database server, and Apache AGE adds graph queries to Postgres.Outside open-source projects.
fxtwitter / faster-whisper distil-large-v3 fxtwitter is a public API that returns X posts without login. faster-whisper distil-large-v3 is a local speech-to-text model we ran on the GPU to transcribe recordings.Outside services and open-source tools, used in the Horthy sweep.
Graphify (graphifyy) Open-source Python tool that builds a knowledge graph from a mixed corpus using tree-sitter. Its 71.5x S claim compares tokens per graph query with reading every raw file. Used as a comparator arm.Outside project safishamsi/graphify; PyPI package graphifyy.
Graphiti / Mem0 / Letta / Zep / Copilot Memory Outside agent-memory products we studied for ideas (two clocks, retire rather than delete, re-check when used) and for their failure modes.Outside companies and open-source projects, studied in the knowledge-store research.
GraphRAG / HippoRAG / RepoGraph / LocAgent / Aider repo-map Outside systems that use graphs to help models retrieve or locate code, cited as prior art with mixed results. Aider's repo-map is a tree-sitter outline ranked by personalised PageRank.Outside research papers and the Aider tool, as cited in our graph-test research.
HumanLayer Dex Horthy's company, behind the repositories, docs and talks that fed the sweep. It joined Factory on 2026-11-04.Outside company; the Factory move is confirmed in the Horthy sweep.
Kyle Mistele A second author, separate from Dex Horthy, who added skills to the HumanLayer repositories and gave a talk on loop engineering; 97 M of the 1,906 M sweep cards come from Kyle Mistele’s material.Outside person whose material appears in HumanLayer repositories and talks.
LadybugDB / Kuzu LadybugDB 0.22.3 S is an embedded graph database, a maintained fork of Kuzu, whose upstream was archived in 2025. It was one graph-engine arm of the test.Open-source projects; archive status as read in our graph-test research.
Lethal trifecta The prompt-injection risk that appears when one agent has untrusted content, private data and a way to communicate outside at the same time.Named by Simon Willison; appears in Horthy's material.
Maestro An open-source mobile UI test tool that drives app screens from scripted flows. We proposed it for on-device smoke tests; it is a proposal, not a measured part of the gates.Outside open-source tool, named in our skills packages and orchestration design.
Matt Pocock A TypeScript educator, known for Total TypeScript. A Matt Pocock livestream is one of the Dex Horthy sweep’s sources.Outside person; HARNESS-IDEAS-HORTHY-2026-11.md.
Memoization / case-based reasoning / KEDB / KCS / elastic-recheck Memoization: reusing earlier answers. Case-based reasoning: solving by retrieving similar past cases. KEDB: known-error database. KCS: knowledge-centred service. elastic-recheck: OpenStack's tool matching failures to known-bug queries.Computer science; Aamodt and Plaza 1994; ITIL practice; OpenStack.
MemTree / LCM / Virtual Context / YesMem / Cairn / Headroom / squeez / context-mode / claude-mem / CCH Outside memory, compression and context-capping tools the clinic survey audited. Each limits only part of what enters the window; we adopted none.Outside projects.
METR An outside study of 16 S developers in early 2025 that found AI access raised task completion time by 19 percent S.METR, an outside research group.
Neo4j A widely used graph database server (runs on the JVM). It was a candidate engine for the graph test but was not installed.Neo4j, Inc.
Predictive test selection Facebook's learned method for choosing which tests to run for a change, cited as outside evidence for selective checking.Machalica et al., ICSE-SEIP 2019.
Promptfoo / Langfuse / Phoenix Open-source tools for evaluating and tracing language-model runs.Outside open-source projects.
Pydantic AI / Instructor / TypeChat / DSPy / GEPA Outside frameworks cited as prior art: offline test models, schema checks with bounded repair, and prompt optimisation. GEPA (Genetic Pareto) is DSPy's optimiser.Outside open-source projects (TypeChat from Microsoft; GEPA from the DSPy authors).
Ralph loop Running an agent in a repeating loop on a task until it is done, rather than in a single session.Geoff Huntley's technique; Dex Horthy discussed and debated it in talks.
ReasoningBank / Gloaguen et al. ReasoningBank stores distilled lessons from agent failures and cut SWE-bench steps by 4-9 % S. Gloaguen et al. found repository context files raise cost over 20 % S without general success gains.Outside research papers, cited in the knowledge-store design.
RPI (research-plan-implement) A three-stage working method: research the code first, write a plan, then implement it. HumanLayer ships it as a plugin.Dex Horthy and HumanLayer (their riptide-rpi plugin and skills).
RRF / doc2query / sqlite-vec / bge-small RRF: reciprocal rank fusion of rankings. doc2query: paraphrases generated and added at write time. sqlite-vec: a vector extension for SQLite. bge-small: a small local embedding model.Information-retrieval research and open-source projects.
Schema-aligned parsing (SAP) BAML's method of putting the schema in the prompt and then repairing the model's reply to fit it. Our harness rejects a bad reply instead.BoundaryML (blog post, 2024).
SlopCodeBench An outside benchmark of how maintainable agent-written code stays over successive features. Horthy's October 2026 report found medium effort often matched or beat xhigh at lower cost, from one run per setting.Outside study (Gabe Orlanski), reported by Dex Horthy.
Software factory The idea of automated code-production loops. Horthy's talk argues there is no software factory without better verifiers.Dex Horthy's essays and keynote (2026-09-17) and AGNTCon talk (2026-10-22).
SWE-bench Lite An outside benchmark of real GitHub issues for coding agents. We cite it for fix-selection methods: voting alone among candidate patches resolved 25.7 % S.Outside benchmark, cited from the papers in our bottleneck research.
TanStack DB / Cloudflare R2 / cloudflared / Caddy / Dependabot / VPS / git-shell / MSIX Outside tools named in skills and the store design: offline-sync library, object storage, tunnel, web server, dependency updater, rented server, restricted git login shell, Windows app packaging.Outside vendors and open-source projects.
Tessl episode, AGNTCon talk, <important if> Tessl: a podcast episode read in the addendum. AGNTCon conference talk of 2026-10-22: 'There Is No Software Factory Without Better Verifiers', but we found no recording, so we did not guess at its content. <important if>: Horthy's March 2026 tag for conditional rules.Outside sources, from Dex Horthy's talks, podcasts and writing.
Tree / Forest / Graph of Thoughts Prompting schemes where the model writes several partial answers, then branches, votes or merges them. Reported gains were on puzzles with a 2023 model; not yet re-tested on current models.Outside research papers.
tree-sitter / ast-grep tree-sitter is a local code parser covering about 40 S languages. ast-grep searches code by syntax tree, built on it.Outside open-source projects.

General software terms

Allow-list A list of permitted forms (citation styles, tools) so legitimate items are not flagged or refused.General security and configuration practice.
Amdahl-style bound The ceiling on speed-up when only part of the work can be removed: if a share X of the time is removed, the best speed-up is 1/(1-X).Amdahl's law, from computer architecture.
Atomic rename Replacing a file by writing the new version beside it and renaming it over the old one in a single step, so anything reading the file sees either the whole old version or the whole new one, never half of each.Standard file-system practice; FixFlow’s gate scripts land changes this way so a running lane never reads a half-written script.
B+ tree A balanced search tree used by databases. Inner nodes hold only keys that route a search and all data sits in the leaves; a node that outgrows its size splits in two, and small neighbours merge.Database systems, 1970s; in the database lectures on our list (MTH-67).
Backend gate tools (Alembic, ruff, mypy, lint-imports, pytest, pip-audit) Migrations, lint and format, type check, import-boundary check, tests, and an advisory dependency vulnerability scan.Outside open-source Python tools.
BM25 / IDF / IDF-weighted coverage BM25 is a word-matching formula whose scores only order results within one query. IDF weights rare words. IDF-weighted coverage is the share of a query's rare-word weight an entry matches.Information-retrieval field; BM25 is built into SQLite FTS5.
Branch A named line of commits that a slice or lane works on, kept apart from the main line until the work is reviewed and merged.Git; each lane and slice gets its own branch and worktree.
Call graph / blast radius / touch list A call graph maps which functions call which. Blast radius, or touch list, is the set of functions, callers, importers, co-changing files and tests a fix could affect, attached to a reviewer brief.General software practice; the script is proposed in HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS section 6.
chars/4 A rule-of-thumb token estimate (characters divided by 4) that undercounts by about 25-35 percent E in this repository.A common rule of thumb.
CI Continuous integration: the automated checks that run on the repository (GitHub Actions, pinned to Node 22).General software practice.
Co-change How often two files change in the same commit, used as a hint that they belong together. In the graph test it reached precision 0.26 M in a list of ten.Software-evolution research; measured in our graph test.
Commit One saved, named change to the code in git. Reviews bind to a specific commit, and a finding closes on a commit.Git; our verdicts name the head commit they were made on.
Community prior / Louvain A stored grouping of related nodes, found by Louvain community detection, added to the ranking as a prior.General graph-algorithm field.
Connected components / k-core Two graph measures. Connected components are groups of nodes linked to one another; the k-core is the part of a graph where every node has at least k links, its densely connected centre.Standard graph algorithms.
Content-hash id / canonical JSON A file named by the sha256 of its own sorted-key JSON bytes, so replaying an event is harmless. SHA-256 is the fingerprint used to pin versions.General content-addressing practice.
Context window Everything the model sees on one call: system prompt, tools, earlier messages and results. With our compaction setting the practical ceiling is near 367k tokens M.General language-model field.
Covering index A database index that holds every column a query needs, so the query is answered from the index without reading the table.Standard database practice.
Cypher The query language of graph databases such as Neo4j and LadybugDB: a query describes a pattern of nodes and links to find.Created for Neo4j; now the openCypher standard.
Egress Data leaving the machine to an outside service, here the model provider.General security term.
Escape hatch An allowed value such as UNVERIFIABLE or unknown that lets an agent say the input does not fit, instead of inventing an answer.General prompt-engineering practice.
Fail open / fail closed What a check does when it breaks. Fail open lets the action through; fail closed refuses it. Our edit hook fails open so a broken hook never blocks work; the privacy scrubber fails closed so nothing unscrubbed is written.Standard reliability and security terms.
Fail-before / pass-after A fix is evidenced by a test that fails (by assertion) on the base commit and passes on the head commit.General testing practice; our stricter form comes from Horthy's material.
Git bundle A single file holding a repository's history, usable as an off-machine backup.A git feature.
Graph engine Software that stores nodes and edges and answers multi-hop queries natively, such as LadybugDB or DuckDB with graph support. Under test against SQLite.Graph-test research; engine choice is my pending install decision.
Head SHA / base SHA The git commit id at the tip of a branch (head) or where it branched (base). A reviewer's verdict is bound to the head SHA it read.Git.
Hop One link step in a graph; three hops reaches things three links away from the starting point.Graph theory.
Hub / metapath Hub: a file many others depend on. Metapath: a typed route through the graph, such as calls, client URL, route, handler, then table write.General graph field.
Jest / Vitest Test runners for the mobile code (Jest) and the web code (Vitest).Open-source JavaScript tools.
JSON Schema (additionalProperties:false) A typed shape for agent output. The additionalProperties:false setting forbids extra fields, and a description keyword attaches plain-language meaning to a property.Outside standard (JSON Schema).
Knowledge graph / temporal knowledge graph (TKG) A graph where a model reads text and code and writes meaning into it. A TKG also records when each fact became true and was superseded. Our parser-built graph was neither.General AI field; outside systems such as Graphiti and Zep implement it.
Lock-removal experiment / race test Removing one lock to prove the named test then fails. A race test runs two concurrent actions to prove a lock stops the conflict.Used in the clinic gate; general concurrency testing.
Locust / query count (N+1) / fsync=off Locust is an open-source load tester. N+1 is a page issuing many small database queries. fsync=off is a Postgres setting that skips disk flushes, safe only for disposable test databases.Outside open-source projects and database practice.
Main line (main) The branch holding the accepted state of the code. Work merges into it only after the check and a review; a deploy is cut from it.Git convention; FixFlow's default branch is main.
Merge Bringing a reviewed branch into the main line. In harness v2 a script does it, through the merge queue, after one check.Git; harness v2 mechanism that removes root edits at merge.
node:sqlite / WAL / BEGIN IMMEDIATE / busy_timeout Node's built-in SQLite module (release candidate) and the settings that let many readers and one writer share a file safely and wait briefly when it is busy.Node.js and SQLite.
Output tokens Tokens the model writes, including thinking. In the token study, 45 % M of them were thinking.General language-model field.
P0, P1, P2, P3 (severity) Finding severity from most to least serious. In the testbed, late P1 fixes sometimes created new defects, and many P3 ids were carried without a status.Common triage convention; the scheme is used in the G2 gate and clinic reviews.
PageRank / personalised PageRank A ranking that scores a node higher when well-linked nodes point to it. The personalised version restarts from a seed file so scores favour its neighbourhood. Aider's repo-map uses it.Google's web-search ranking algorithm; used in the Aider tool.
pg_stat_activity A built-in Postgres view that lists the open sessions and what each one is waiting on.PostgreSQL.
Playwright A browser automation tool that can drive a web app and take screenshots.Outside open-source project (Microsoft).
Property graph / symbol-level graph A graph whose nodes and links each carry a kind and evidence (file and line). Symbol-level means nodes are functions, classes and components rather than whole files.General graph-database and code-analysis field.
Pull request (PR) A proposal on GitHub to merge a branch into main, with its changes, discussion and checks. Several of our design documents live as numbered PRs.GitHub; see PR #182 to #186.
Red-team Deliberate adversarial testing of a mechanism to find how it fails; eight M red-team defects were still open.Security field practice.
RPO / RTO Recovery point objective (how much data may be lost) and recovery time objective (how long recovery may take).Disaster-recovery field.
Serial pass / pytest-xdist pytest-xdist runs tests in parallel workers. The serial pass is a second run for tests that cannot run in parallel, such as race tests.pytest-xdist is an open-source pytest plugin; the serial pass is our usage.
SQLite / FTS5 / recursive query SQLite is a small file-based database. FTS5 is its built-in full-text search with BM25 ranking. A recursive query follows links over several steps.Open-source SQLite project.
Squash merge / cherry-pick / patch-id Squash merge lands a PR as one commit; cherry-pick copies a commit onto another branch; patch-id hashes a change so it still matches after squashing.Git and GitHub features.
Stampede / single-flight / claim / fencing token / Lamport counter Stampede: several sessions repeating costly work. Claim: the first proceeds. Fencing token (claim_seq): marks a stale holder. Lamport counter: orders events from several writers.Caching practice; Martin Kleppmann (fencing); Leslie Lamport (logical clocks).
tmux A terminal tool that runs several shell sessions in one window. One program can read or type into another’s session, which is how one Claude session can watch another.Outside open-source tool.
Token The unit of text a model reads or writes. Usage, cost and window size are all counted in tokens.General language-model field.
Tracing (test start-up) Recording where a program spends its time, step by step, so the slow part can be found and cut. Tracing the clinic’s test start-up showed what to cut and made start-up 3.7× faster M.General software practice, also called profiling; used in the clinic testbed’s faster-check work.
Trees (event and fault trees) A view listing every route from start to outcome, with its chance and cost on each branch.Reliability engineering; proposed by me for the pathway map.
uv A fast Python package and environment manager. A throwaway uv environment is made for one job and deleted afterwards, so nothing is installed on the system.Outside open-source tool (Astral).
Worktree A separate checked-out working copy of a git repository on its own branch, one per slice or lane session (19 M existed on this PC).A git feature.

The machine

adb / dumpsys / logcat / apksigner / aapt2 / JDK Android tools: adb talks to a phone; dumpsys and logcat read state and logs; apksigner checks signing; aapt2 reads APK info; a JDK runs Gradle.Google Android SDK; Temurin JDK build.
Android emulator / AVD ff34 A software phone for tests. ff34 is the one virtual device set up on this PC (Android 14, 2 GB S RAM).Google Android tools; the device name is ours.
ANGLE Google’s graphics translation layer, which turns one kind of graphics call into another, for example OpenGL into DirectX. One of the Android emulator’s GPU modes draws through it.Google open-source project, used by the Android emulator.
Antivirus (360 Total Security) The third-party real-time scanner on this PC, which has blocked some DLLs (Windows library files) during unpacking and so affects installs.Third-party security product from Qihoo 360.
AppData virtualisation Windows can give a packaged app, such as the Claude desktop app, and the processes it starts their own private view of some AppData folders. Files written there can then differ from what my own shell sees at the same path, so a shared store must live elsewhere.Windows MSIX app packaging; found as KS-F1 in the knowledge-store design.
core.longpaths A git setting that lets Git for Windows create files whose full path is longer than Windows’ old limit of 260 characters. We pass it per command (git -c core.longpaths=true) when cloning into scratch folders.Git for Windows.
Docker / container / Docker Desktop / WSL2 / Compose project Docker runs isolated environments. Docker Desktop runs Linux containers inside WSL2, a Linux virtual machine on Windows that holds much of this PC's memory. A Compose project is containers started together.Docker Inc. and Microsoft.
Emulator GPU modes (-gpu host, swiftshader_indirect) Settings for how the Android emulator draws the phone screen: host uses the PC’s graphics card; swiftshader_indirect draws in software on the processor, slower but independent of the graphics driver.Android emulator command-line options (Google).
Job object A Windows feature that kills a whole process tree when its owner dies.Microsoft Windows.
Kernel-Power Event 41 / bugcheck A Windows log entry for a restart without clean shutdown (24 M on this PC). A bugcheck is a crash with a stop code; 23 of 24 M had code 0.Microsoft Windows.
KVM (/dev/kvm, svm flag) Linux’s built-in hardware virtualisation. /dev/kvm is the device a Linux system needs to run a fast virtual machine such as the Android emulator; the svm flag shows an AMD processor supports it. Docker’s Linux VM on this PC does not expose it, so the emulator runs on Windows.Linux kernel feature; found in the device-lab work (ship plan §7.5).
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV A Git Bash setting that stops it rewriting arguments that look like Unix paths into Windows paths. With it set, paths are written as C:/… .MSYS2, the Unix layer under Git for Windows.
Network namespace sharing A Docker option that lets the gates container use the database container's network, so the database appears at localhost.Docker feature.
Node 22 / Node 24 Two versions of the JavaScript runtime. The project targets 22 and the machine has 24.Node.js project.
Page cache Memory an operating system keeps for recently read files. On this PC the Docker VM held gigabytes of it that Windows could not use.General operating-system concept.
Peak memory The most memory one check uses at its worst moment. It was never measured; the second check slot waits on it.Bottleneck B07: slots are to be sized from one measured number.
Rented host A server rented for one day to rehearse deployment and rerun the load drill, using made-up data only.Bottlenecks B19 and B20; free steps come first.
Sensor logger A small tool recording power, temperature and memory on the PC so the unexpected shutdowns can be diagnosed from data. I allowed a sensor logger and a debugger (decision D05).Bottleneck B05; harness v2 phase 1.
SetThreadExecutionState / hybrid sleep / mains / BitLocker A Windows call that prevents sleep while a program runs. Hybrid sleep saves memory to disk before sleeping. Mains is wall power. BitLocker is Windows disk encryption.Microsoft Windows; electrical supply term.
TIME_WAIT / error 10055 A Windows socket state, and the 'No buffer space available' error seen on loopback connections.Windows networking.
Windows check The check run directly on Windows rather than in a Linux container. Slower (6.1 minutes M) and hit by the loopback socket error; the container run is the faster route.Bottleneck work on the gate; compare the container run at 3.8 minutes M.
Windows Hypervisor Platform (WHPX) A Windows feature that lets an Android emulator run hardware-accelerated without /dev/kvm.Microsoft Windows.

Measurement and statistics

95 % interval The range expected to hold the true value in 95 of 100 repeats of a test. A difference smaller than the interval cannot be told from noise.Statistics; used with the bootstrap in the held-out graph test.
Cluster bootstrap / sign-flip test A 95 % S interval from 10,000 S resamples by commit, and a permutation test for paired differences between arms.General statistics.
Leave-one-handle-out A calibration that removes one lookup key from an entry and checks the entry can still be found.Information-retrieval evaluation style; named in knowledge-store research lane T-03.
Monte Carlo runs (ensemble) Running a model many times with each unknown drawn from its range, to see the spread of outcomes and which unknowns matter most, instead of one answer.General statistics; I proposed it for the library pathway map.
MRR / nDCG@10 / AUC Rank-quality scores: mean reciprocal rank, normalised discounted cumulative gain at ten, and area under the recall-against-tokens curve.Information-retrieval field.
P@1 / recall at shown / acted false positive P@1: precision of the top result. Recall at shown: how many true entries appear in what is displayed. Acted false positive: a wrong lead someone acted on.Information-retrieval metrics; applied in the knowledge-store design.
p50 / p95 (percentiles) Response-time percentiles. p50 is the median: half of the requests are faster. p95 is the time that 95 % of requests beat, so it shows the slow tail.Standard performance-testing statistics.
Positive control A case that must be detected, proving the check can find something. Every check that reports nothing found needs one.Scientific method (laboratory and statistical practice).
Recall / precision / recall@8k Recall: share of true items found. Precision: share of returned items that are true. recall@8k: share of reference items inside an 8,000-token S answer, the graph test's main score.Information-retrieval field.
Rolling-origin test Repeating a held-out test at several split dates: each time, tune on the commits before the date and score on the commits after it, to see whether a result holds over time rather than for one split.Time-series forecasting practice (rolling-origin evaluation).
Rule of three / Clopper-Pearson bound Bounds on a rate from few trials: zero failures in n trials puts the true rate under about 3/n, so 0 in 40 gives 7.5 % S. Clopper-Pearson gives the exact one-sided bound.Statistics field.
Spearman rank correlation A statistic showing how steadily one number rises or falls as another rises across runs; used to rank which unknowns move a result most.General statistics, named for Charles Spearman.
TUNE / HELD-OUT split The 65 S June commits used to choose settings (tune) and the 75 S July-August commits scored once for the verdict (held-out).General machine-learning practice; split defined in graph2/protocol.md.

System dynamics

Knee The lane or worker count where the lowest limit is reached. Beyond it, more lanes or workers add queues and tokens but no speed. In the testbed the check’s knee was between 6 and 12 workers M, and about three lanes M were worth running.Capacity-planning and queueing practice.
Loops R1-R4, B1-B5 Reinforcing (R) and balancing (B) feedback loops. R1 fix spiral, R2 context growth, R3 library compounds, R4 pile-up. B1 check capacity, B2 serial gate, B3 limit stop, B4 staleness, B5 lanes at knee.System dynamics method; the loops are named by us in the harness v2 design.
Stocks and flows Model quantities (stocks, such as slices waiting) and the rates that move them between states (flows).System dynamics.
System dynamics A way of modelling a system as stocks (things that pile up, such as waiting work), flows (rates in and out) and feedback loops, then running the model over time to see where queues form and what a change would do. We use it for the harness and the library, with loops R1 to R4 and B1 to B5.A modelling method begun by Jay Forrester at MIT in the 1950s. Harness v2 and the library pathway map use it, because I asked to see the system as stocks, flows and loops with a runnable model.

FixFlow

ASVS / MASVS / SRB / FBR / NOT VALID then VALIDATE OWASP security checklists for web and mobile apps; Sindh Revenue Board and Federal Board of Revenue (Pakistan taxes); a Postgres pattern that adds a constraint without scanning, then validates rows later.OWASP; Pakistan tax authorities; PostgreSQL.
Bare app / config plugins Expo terms. A managed app lets Expo generate the native Android project at build time; a bare app keeps its own native folder, and Expo then skips its config plugins, the build-time add-ons that set permissions and native settings.Expo (outside open-source tool); FixFlow build traps.
CODE-MAP.md A hand-written map of where each capability lives in each runtime of the FixFlow repository.FixFlow repository docs (docs/CODE-MAP.md).
Expo / EAS / APK / expo prebuild / Gradle / assembleRelease Expo: the React Native toolkit. EAS: its build service. APK: the Android install file. expo prebuild generates native folders (kept out of the repo). Gradle's assembleRelease builds a release APK.Expo; Google Android.
expo-updates Expo’s over-the-air update feature, which can push new JavaScript to installed apps without a new build. FixFlow’s device rulings say not to use it.Expo (outside open-source tool); FixFlow ship-plan rulings.
FastAPI The Python web framework behind the FixFlow backend, with async SQLAlchemy and Alembic. Named here because the backend gate steps run against it.CLAUDE.md stack table; Python 3.12 backend.
FixFlow The workshop management product for a Karachi home-appliance repair shop. Its repository is where this harness work lives, and it is one of the two measured projects.My project; this repository.
Fleet APK v1 / v2 / deploy train / T_close v1: the first drain build, with P2a and P2b-1 only. v2: built after P4c. Deploy train: behaviour-changing PRs merged before cutover. T_close: the end of the cutover window.Coined by us in the ship plan, 2026-11.
Geofence A location boundary around the shop. When a technician’s phone crosses it, the FixFlow app prompts an arrival or exit punch for attendance, even in the background.Mobile location practice; FixFlow technician app (CLAUDE.md, Mobile).
Handoff / HANDOFF register docs/HANDOFF-2026-07-28-open-work.md: the earlier document of open work, whose list of known defects we used as a baseline.Our repository docs (written 2026-07-28).
Kacha khata / pakka khata Urdu bookkeeping terms: the informal operational ledger (the app) versus the formal approved ledger that flows to Odoo.Urdu bookkeeping terms I use.
Lane names (B-core, B-jobs, B-att, B-tools, M, W, O, L, OWN) Ship-plan work areas: B-core backend core, B-jobs jobs and money, B-att attendance, B-tools scripts, M mobile, W web, O ops, L lab, OWN my own steps.Coined by us in SHIP-PLAN-2026-11, section 7.3.
Odoo / JSON-2 / External IDs Odoo is accounting software that receives the approved ledger. JSON-2 is its newer API. External IDs act as the exactly-once key.Outside product (Odoo).
OEM Original equipment manufacturer: here the phone makers (Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo) whose battery policies can stop background apps.General industry term.
Outbox / queues / drain / fleet drain protocol (O-10) / release/drain / hold notice The outbox is the phone's offline queue of unsent writes, never deleted. Drain empties it into the recovered backend by an ordered protocol (O-10) on branch release/drain, after a hold notice telling technicians not to reset the app.FixFlow mobile design (CLAUDE.md); drain and hold notice coined by us in the ship plan.
P0a My pre-flight: hold notice, Railway state, R2 archive, Supabase dump, phone roster and builds. Harness work must not delay it.Coined by us in the ship plan.
Phase ids (P0a, P1, P2a, P7a, P13e ... and L1-L4) Named phases of the ship plan, each sized to fit one session. P is a product phase, L a harness-infrastructure phase (L1 gate harness, L3 device lab); a letter suffix marks a sub-part.Coined by us in the ship plan.
Postgres 16 vs 17 / pg_restore / Appendix C Postgres 16 runs in test containers and 17 matches production. pg_restore restores a dump. Appendix C is the design recipe for a throwaway Postgres 17 restore.PostgreSQL open source; our orchestration design notes.
PR #182 The pull request on the plan branch docs/orchestration-design-2026-10 holding the ship plan, design notes and evidence. It is not merged to main.This repository on GitHub.
Railpack Railway’s automatic build detector: it inspects a folder and decides how to build it. Run from the repository root it finds the web app, which is why the backend is deployed from backend/.Railway (outside vendor); the deploy trap is recorded in CLAUDE.md.
Railway deploy trap Deploying the backend from the repo root rebuilt the API as the web app and caused a production outage. Deploy only from backend/.Our project history, recorded in CLAUDE.md.
Railway, Supabase, R2 (hosts) Railway hosts the apps (old hostnames answer an edge 404). Supabase is managed Postgres, recorded as paused or not answering. Cloudflare R2 stores media and backups.Outside vendors; stack described in CLAUDE.md.
Ruff TID251 / compare_secret TID251 is a Ruff lint rule that bans named APIs such as hmac.compare_digest. compare_secret is our safe secret-compare helper, because the raw call raises on non-ASCII strings.Ruff linter; our own code, per CLAUDE.md.
Sentry A crash-reporting service. The FixFlow mobile app sends crash reports to it only when a DSN, the project’s address, is set.Outside vendor; CLAUDE.md (Mobile).
Session pooler (Supabase) Supabase’s connection proxy. FixFlow’s backend reaches its Postgres database through it over IPv4.Supabase (outside vendor); CLAUDE.md.
Ship plan (SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md) / v6-v9.3 FixFlow's sequenced plan to get shipped, on PR #182. v6 came from the harness review, v7 and v8 from delta checks, v9 added parallel execution, v9.3 delegated merging to the coordinator.Coined by us in docs/program.
testID / accessibilityLabel Labels on React Native screen elements. A test tool such as Maestro finds a button or field by them, and accessibilityLabel also tells screen readers what an element is. The technician app’s source had none when we counted.React Native component properties.
Ticket queue The first-come order of FixFlow’s slot lock (ff-slot.sh): each waiting job drops a ticket and is served in arrival order. A light job may pass a heavier one only until the heavier one has waited 900 s S, so neither kind can starve.docs/program/lab/ff-slot.sh, added on 13 November 2026 after one lane waited 20 minutes M while later arrivals were served.

How this compile was made

I followed our orchestration design. Sonnet agents first extracted every idea, bottleneck and term from the sources without judging them, each record with a citation in the form path:line — quote. I merged duplicates and sorted the records into themes and work packages. Fresh-context Opus agents then checked all 469 M condensed idea records, and every number in the narrative, against the sources; they split out 10 M more where one record had swallowed a second idea, and I set aside one record about FixFlow’s own product features, which gives the 478 M ideas in Part 3. 268 M idea records and 11 M narrative claims were corrected or tightened, and the corrected text is what is printed here. Last, nine fresh-context readers read the draft as a newcomer would and raised 317 M points on clarity, numbers and tone; I applied nearly all of them. Where the record does not know something, this compile says so. Throughout, “I” is me and “we” is the team. What changed on 14 November. I changed the lens to the seven metrics and asked for the ideas that lived only in chat. Agents read all 376 M messages I typed in 59 M saved sessions and matched 113 M ideas, observations and requests against the records: 5 M were missing and are now recorded, and one measurement that no record held (MSR-50) joins them: six new ideas, 484 M in all. Eight classifier agents sorted all 606 M earlier records by metric and cause, and a blind second reading agreed on the main metric for 80 of 101 M. Idea records otherwise describe where things stood on 13 November, except those of the split idea (PAR-22, TOK-44, TOK-02, TK-FILL, TK-SUMMARIES, PR-HALLU and package WP12), which carry what WP12 finished on 14 November: the rule, its replay and the set-up of the trial I approved.
